primitives.name: Feedback Control Loop
primitives.verbatim_quote: This control of a machine on the basis of its actual performance rather than its expected performance is known as feedback, and involves sensory members which are actuated by motor members and perform the function of tell-tales or monitors — that is, of elements which indicate a performance.
primitives.assumptions: System operates in closed-loop with continuous measurement and adjustment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Loss of feedback causes open-loop instability or overshoot.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core concept of feedback control emerges from the necessity of correcting deviations between desired and actual performance. In the elevator example, merely issuing commands without verifying physical location introduces risk. Feedback ensures alignment between intended and realized states. The mathematical structure underpinning this is a closed-loop system: y(t) = f(r(t), e(t)), where r(t) is reference, e(t) = r(t) - y(t) is error, and u(t) = g(e(t)) is corrective action. Sensorimotor integration extends this to biological systems, where kinaesthetic feedback allows precise motor control. Adaptive behavior generalizes this to environments where static policies fail, requiring dynamic adjustments based on outcome signals. These primitives form a hierarchy: sensorimotor → feedback → adaptive behavior, each layer enabling robustness against environmental variability.
